public delegate void RegisterBlowDelegate(Mission mission, Agent attacker, Agent victim, WeakGameEntity realHitEntity, Blow b, ref AttackCollisionData collisionData, in MissionWeapon attackerWeapon, ref CombatLogData combatLogData);

public class CustomAttacksUtils
{
    public static BlowDirection GetDirectionOfBlow(Agent victim, Vec3 blowOrigin)
    {
        Vec3 victimLookDirection = victim.GetMovementDirection().ToVec3();
        Vec3 victimToBlowOrigin = (blowOrigin - victim.Position).NormalizedCopy();
        float angleInRadians = (float)Math.Atan2(
            victimLookDirection.x * victimToBlowOrigin.y - victimLookDirection.y * victimToBlowOrigin.x,
            victimLookDirection.x * victimToBlowOrigin.x + victimLookDirection.y * victimToBlowOrigin.y);
        float angleInDegrees = (float)(angleInRadians * (180f / Math.PI));

        if (angleInDegrees < -135 && angleInDegrees > -180)
            return BlowDirection.Back;
        else if (angleInDegrees < -45 && angleInDegrees > -135)
            return BlowDirection.Right;
        else if (angleInDegrees < 45 && angleInDegrees > -45)
            return BlowDirection.Front;
        else if (angleInDegrees > 45 && angleInDegrees < 135)
            return BlowDirection.Left;
        else
            return BlowDirection.Back;
    }

    private static readonly RegisterBlowDelegate _registerBlow;
    private static readonly bool _initializationFailed;
    private static readonly string _initializationError;

    static CustomAttacksUtils()
    {
        try
        {
            var parameterTypes = new Type[]
            {
                typeof(Agent),
                typeof(Agent),
                typeof(WeakGameEntity),
                typeof(Blow),
                typeof(AttackCollisionData).MakeByRefType(),
                typeof(MissionWeapon).MakeByRefType(),
                typeof(CombatLogData).MakeByRefType()
            };

            MethodInfo blowMethod = typeof(Mission).GetMethod(
                "RegisterBlow",
                BindingFlags.Instance | BindingFlags.NonPublic,
                null,
                parameterTypes,
                null);

            if (blowMethod == null)
            {
                _initializationFailed = true;
                _initializationError = "Mission.RegisterBlow method not found with expected signature";
                TaleWorlds.Library.Debug.Print($"[TAOM] CustomAttacksUtils: {_initializationError}", 0, TaleWorlds.Library.Debug.DebugColor.Red);
                return;
            }

            _registerBlow = (RegisterBlowDelegate)Delegate.CreateDelegate(typeof(RegisterBlowDelegate), null, blowMethod);
            TaleWorlds.Library.Debug.Print("[TAOM] CustomAttacksUtils: RegisterBlow delegate created successfully", 0, TaleWorlds.Library.Debug.DebugColor.Green);
        }
        catch (Exception ex)
        {
            _initializationFailed = true;
            _initializationError = $"Failed to create RegisterBlow delegate: {ex.Message}";
            TaleWorlds.Library.Debug.Print($"[TAOM] CustomAttacksUtils: {_initializationError}", 0, TaleWorlds.Library.Debug.DebugColor.Red);
        }
    }

    public static void RegisterBlow(Agent attacker, Agent victim, WeakGameEntity realHitEntity, Blow b, ref AttackCollisionData collisionData, in MissionWeapon attackerWeapon, ref CombatLogData combatLogData)
    {
        if (_initializationFailed || _registerBlow == null)
        {
            TaleWorlds.Library.Debug.Print($"[TAOM] CustomAttacksUtils.RegisterBlow: Skipped - initialization failed: {_initializationError ?? "delegate is null"}", 0, TaleWorlds.Library.Debug.DebugColor.Yellow);
            return;
        }
        _registerBlow(Mission.Current, attacker, victim, realHitEntity, b, ref collisionData, in attackerWeapon, ref combatLogData);
    }

    public static void TakeDamage(Agent victim, int damage, float magnitude = 50f, bool knockDown = false)
    {
        TakeDamage(victim, victim, damage, magnitude, knockDown);
    }

    public static void TakeDamage(Agent victim, Agent attacker, int damage, float magnitude = 50f, bool knockDown = false)
    {
        if (victim == null || attacker == null || victim.Health <= 0) return;

        Blow blow = new(attacker.Index)
        {
            DamageType = DamageTypes.Pierce,
            BoneIndex = victim.Monster.HeadLookDirectionBoneIndex,
            GlobalPosition = (attacker.Position + victim.Position) * 0.5f
        };
        blow.GlobalPosition.z += victim.GetEyeGlobalHeight();
        blow.BaseMagnitude = magnitude;
        blow.WeaponRecord.FillAsMeleeBlow(null, null, -1, -1);
        blow.InflictedDamage = damage;
        blow.SwingDirection = victim.LookDirection;
        MatrixFrame frame = victim.Frame;
        blow.SwingDirection = frame.rotation.TransformToParent(new Vec3(-1f, 0f, 0f, -1f));
        blow.SwingDirection.Normalize();
        blow.Direction = blow.SwingDirection;
        blow.DamageCalculated = true;
        if (knockDown)
        {
            if (victim.HasMount) blow.BlowFlag |= BlowFlags.CanDismount;
            else blow.BlowFlag |= BlowFlags.KnockDown;
        }

        sbyte mainHandItemBoneIndex = attacker.Monster.MainHandItemBoneIndex;
        // The 3 positional ints below map to (affectorWeaponSlotOrMissileIndex,
        // StrikeType, DamageType). DamageType MUST match blow.DamageType — vanilla's
        // combat-log message generator reads the collision data's DamageType, not the
        // Blow's, so a mismatch makes hits read "Blunt" in the in-game log even when
        // the Blow correctly says Pierce. LOTRAOM had this set to `2` (Blunt), which
        // was a long-standing bug that only became visible once warg bites started
        // landing reliably (post-cc9e0c4). See plan file 2026-05-27.
        AttackCollisionData attackCollisionDataForDebugPurpose = AttackCollisionData.GetAttackCollisionDataForDebugPurpose(
            false, false, false, true, false, false, false, false, false, false, false, false,
            CombatCollisionResult.StrikeAgent,
            -1, 0, (int)DamageTypes.Pierce,
            blow.BoneIndex,
            BoneBodyPartType.Abdomen,
            mainHandItemBoneIndex,
            UsageDirection.AttackLeft,
            -1,
            CombatHitResultFlags.NormalHit,
            0.5f, 1f, 0f, 0f, 0f, 0f, 0f, 0f,
            Vec3.Up,
            blow.Direction,
            blow.GlobalPosition,
            Vec3.Zero,
            Vec3.Zero,
            victim.Velocity,
            Vec3.Up
        );

        CombatLogData combatLogData = new(false, attacker.IsHuman, attacker.IsMine, attacker.RiderAgent != null, attacker.RiderAgent != null && attacker.RiderAgent.IsMine, attacker.IsMount, victim.IsHuman, victim.IsMine, victim.Health <= 0f, victim.RiderAgent != null, victim.RiderAgent != null && victim.RiderAgent.IsMine, victim.IsMount, null, victim.RiderAgent == victim, knockDown, false, 0f);
        MissionWeapon weapon = MissionWeapon.Invalid;
        RegisterBlow(attacker, victim, WeakGameEntity.Invalid, blow, ref attackCollisionDataForDebugPurpose, in weapon, ref combatLogData);
    }
}
using TAOM.Adapters;
using TAOM.Core.Logging;
using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using TaleWorlds.Engine;
using TaleWorlds.Library;

namespace TAOM.Features.AdvancedCombat;

public class BoneCheck
{
    private static IModLogger Logger => IoC.Resolve<IModLogger>();
    protected IAgentAdapter _agent;
    protected List<IAgentAdapter> _targets;
    protected List<sbyte> _boneIds;
    protected float _collisionRadiusSquared;
    protected float _maxRangeForCheck;
    protected float _maxDuration;
    protected bool _stopOnFirstHit;
    protected float _boneCheckLifeTime = 0f;
    protected Action<IAgentAdapter, IAgentAdapter, sbyte> _onCollisionCallback;
    protected Action _onExpiration;

    public BoneCheck(IAgentAdapter agent, List<IAgentAdapter> targets, List<sbyte> boneIds, float maxDuration, float boneCollisionRadius, bool stopAfterFirstHit, Action<IAgentAdapter, IAgentAdapter, sbyte> onCollisionCallback, Action onExpiration)
    {
        _agent = agent;
        _targets = targets;
        _boneIds = boneIds;
        _collisionRadiusSquared = boneCollisionRadius * boneCollisionRadius;
        _maxRangeForCheck = Math.Max(20f, _collisionRadiusSquared * 20f);
        _maxDuration = maxDuration;
        _stopOnFirstHit = stopAfterFirstHit;
        _onCollisionCallback = onCollisionCallback;
        _onExpiration = onExpiration;
    }

    public virtual bool Tick(float dt)
    {
        _boneCheckLifeTime += dt;
        if (_boneCheckLifeTime >= _maxDuration)
        {
            _onExpiration?.Invoke();
            return false;
        }
        if (!CheckBoneCollision())
        {
            _onExpiration?.Invoke();
            return false;
        }
        return true;
    }

    protected bool CheckBoneCollision()
    {
        if (_agent == null || !_agent.IsActive() || _agent.IsFadingOut())
        {
            Logger.LogWarning($"Agent {_agent?.Name ?? "null"} is no longer valid for bone collision check");
            return false;
        }

        IAgentVisualsAdapter agentVisuals = _agent.AgentVisuals;
        if (agentVisuals == null)
        {
            Logger.LogWarning($"Failed to get visuals for {_agent.Name}");
            return false;
        }

        Skeleton agentSkeleton = agentVisuals.GetSkeleton();
        if (agentSkeleton == null)
        {
            Logger.LogWarning($"Failed to get skeleton for {_agent.Name}");
            return false;
        }
        MatrixFrame agentGlobalFrame = agentVisuals.GetGlobalFrame();

        List<(sbyte, Vec3)> agentBonePositions = new();
        int boneCount = agentSkeleton.GetBoneCount();
        foreach (sbyte bone in _boneIds)
        {
            if (bone < 0 || bone >= boneCount)
            {
                Logger.LogError($"Invalid bone index {bone} for agent {_agent.Name}");
                continue;
            }
            MatrixFrame agentBoneFrame = agentSkeleton.GetBoneEntitialFrameWithIndex(bone);
            Vec3 agentBoneGlobalPos = agentGlobalFrame.TransformToParent(agentBoneFrame.origin);
            agentBonePositions.Add((bone, agentBoneGlobalPos));
        }

        for (int i = 0; i < _targets.Count; i++)
        {
            IAgentAdapter target = _targets[i];

            if (target == null || !target.IsActive() || target.IsFadingOut())
            {
                _targets.RemoveAt(i);
                i--;
                continue;
            }

            IAgentVisualsAdapter targetVisuals = target.AgentVisuals;
            if (targetVisuals == null)
            {
                _targets.RemoveAt(i);
                i--;
                continue;
            }

            Skeleton targetSkeleton = targetVisuals.GetSkeleton();
            if (targetSkeleton == null)
            {
                _targets.RemoveAt(i);
                i--;
                continue;
            }
            MatrixFrame targetGlobalFrame = targetVisuals.GetGlobalFrame();
            sbyte boneId = FindBoneInRange(agentGlobalFrame, agentBonePositions, targetSkeleton, targetGlobalFrame);
            if (boneId != -1)
            {
                _targets.RemoveAt(i);
                _onCollisionCallback?.Invoke(_agent, target, boneId);
                if (_stopOnFirstHit)
                    return false;
            }
        }
        return true;
    }

    protected sbyte FindBoneInRange(MatrixFrame agentGlobalFrame, List<(sbyte boneId, Vec3 position)> agentBonePositions, Skeleton targetSkeleton, MatrixFrame targetGlobalFrame)
    {
        int targetBoneCount = targetSkeleton.GetBoneCount();
        if ((targetGlobalFrame.origin - agentGlobalFrame.origin).LengthSquared > _maxRangeForCheck)
            return -1;

        for (int i = 0; i < targetBoneCount; i++)
        {
            MatrixFrame targetBoneFrame = targetSkeleton.GetBoneEntitialFrameWithIndex((sbyte)i);
            Vec3 targetBoneGlobalPos = targetGlobalFrame.TransformToParent(targetBoneFrame.origin);
            foreach (var (boneId, agentBonePos) in agentBonePositions)
            {
                float distanceSquared = (targetBoneGlobalPos - agentBonePos).LengthSquared;
                if (distanceSquared <= _collisionRadiusSquared)
                    return (sbyte)i;
            }
        }
        return -1;
    }
}

namespace TAOM.Features.AdvancedCombat;

public class BoneCheckDuringAnimation : BoneCheck
{
    private readonly ActionIndexCache _action;
    private readonly float _actionProgressMin;
    private readonly float _actionProgressMax;

    public BoneCheckDuringAnimation(ActionIndexCache action, IAgentAdapter agent, List<IAgentAdapter> targets, List<sbyte> boneIds, float actionProgressMin, float actionProgressMax, float boneCollisionRadius, bool stopAfterFirstHit, Action<IAgentAdapter, IAgentAdapter, sbyte> onCollisionCallback, Action onExpiration)

        // 0.84m cap on agent-to-agent distance (sqrt(0.7)≈0.84) before bone iteration
        // could even run. At 8-10 m/s the warg crossed that gate in <100ms — usually
        // too narrow a window for the per-frame check to land. Passing 100f (≈10m
        // distance cap) makes the gate a real perf optimization (skip distant agents)
        // instead of an unintended hit-rate killer. Spider attacks use this same

        : base(agent, targets, boneIds, 100f, boneCollisionRadius, stopAfterFirstHit, onCollisionCallback, onExpiration)
    {
        _action = action;
        _actionProgressMin = actionProgressMin;
        _actionProgressMax = actionProgressMax;
    }

    public override bool Tick(float dt)
    {
        if (_agent == null || !_agent.IsActive() || _agent.IsFadingOut())
        {
            _onExpiration?.Invoke();
            return false;
        }

        IAgentVisualsAdapter agentVisuals = _agent.AgentVisuals;
        if (_targets == null || _targets.Count == 0
            || agentVisuals?.GetSkeleton() == null
            || _agent.GetCurrentAction(0) != _action
            || _agent.GetCurrentActionProgress(0) >= _actionProgressMax)
        {
            _onExpiration?.Invoke();
            return false;
        }

        if (_agent.GetCurrentActionProgress(0) >= _actionProgressMin)
        {
            if (!CheckBoneCollision())
            {
                _onExpiration?.Invoke();
                return false;
            }
        }

        return true;
    }
}

using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Linq;
using TAOM.Core.Logging;
using TAOM.Features.AdvancedCombat;
using TAOM.Features.AdvancedCombat.Services;
using TaleWorlds.Core;
using TaleWorlds.Library;
using TaleWorlds.MountAndBlade;

namespace TAOM.Adapters;

public class AgentAdapter : IAgentAdapter
{
    private readonly Agent _agent;
    private readonly IMissionAdapterFactory _factory;
    private readonly IModLogger _logger;
    private readonly Func<IBoneCollisionService> _boneCollisionServiceFactory;

    public AgentAdapter(Agent agent, IMissionAdapterFactory factory, IModLogger logger, Func<IBoneCollisionService> boneCollisionServiceFactory)
    {
        _agent = agent ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(agent));
        _factory = factory ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(factory));
        _logger = logger ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(logger));
        _boneCollisionServiceFactory = boneCollisionServiceFactory ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(boneCollisionServiceFactory));
    }

    public int Index => _agent.Index;

    public IAgentVisualsAdapter AgentVisuals =>
        _agent != null && _agent.IsActive() && !_agent.IsFadingOut() && _agent.AgentVisuals != null
            ? new AgentVisualsAdapter(_agent.AgentVisuals)
            : null;

    public string Name => _agent.Name;
    public bool IsHuman => _agent.IsHuman;
    public bool HasMount => _agent.HasMount;
    public Vec3 Position => _agent.Position;
    public Vec2 MovementVelocity => _agent.MovementVelocity;
    public MatrixFrame Frame => _agent.Frame;
    public bool IsMount => _agent.IsMount;
    public bool IsAIControlled => _agent?.IsAIControlled ?? false;

    public IAgentAdapter RiderAgent =>
        _agent.RiderAgent != null ? _factory.GetAgentAdapter(_agent.RiderAgent) : null;

    public IAgentAdapter MountAgent =>
        _agent.MountAgent != null ? _factory.GetAgentAdapter(_agent.MountAgent) : null;

    public ActionIndexCache GetCurrentAction(int actionChannelNo) => _agent.GetCurrentAction(actionChannelNo);
    public float GetCurrentActionProgress(int actionChannelNo) => _agent.GetCurrentActionProgress(actionChannelNo);

    internal Agent GetUnderlyingAgent() => _agent;

    public bool IsWarg() => _agent.Monster.StringId == "warg";
    public bool IsSpider() => _agent.Monster.StringId == "spider";
    public bool IsHorse() => _agent.Monster.StringId == "horse";
    public bool IsCamel() => _agent.Monster.StringId == "camel";
    public bool IsActive() => _agent?.IsActive() ?? false;
    public bool IsFadingOut() => _agent?.IsFadingOut() ?? false;
    public int Health => (int)(_agent?.Health ?? 0f);
    public AgentState State => _agent?.State ?? AgentState.Killed;

    public bool IsSameTeam(IAgentAdapter other)
    {
        if (other is not AgentAdapter otherImpl) return false;
        var otherAgent = otherImpl.GetUnderlyingAgent();
        if (_agent == null || otherAgent == null) return false;
        return _agent.Team != null && otherAgent.Team != null && _agent.Team == otherAgent.Team;
    }

    public int GetBaseArmorEffectivenessForBodyPart(BoneBodyPartType bodyPart) =>
        (int)(_agent?.GetBaseArmorEffectivenessForBodyPart(bodyPart) ?? 0f);

    public void ProjectAgent(Vec3 position, DamageAnimation animation)
    {
        if (animation == DamageAnimation.Nothing) return;
        if (!_agent.IsHuman || _agent.HasMount) return;

        var blowDirection = CustomAttacksUtils.GetDirectionOfBlow(_agent, position);

        Random random = new();
        string projectionAnimation;
        switch (blowDirection)
        {
            case BlowDirection.Back:
                projectionAnimation = animation == DamageAnimation.Flinch
                    ? HumanAnimationConstants.BackFlinchAnimations[random.Next(0, HumanAnimationConstants.BackFlinchAnimations.Count - 1)]
                    : HumanAnimationConstants.BackFallAnimations[random.Next(0, HumanAnimationConstants.BackFallAnimations.Count - 1)];
                break;
            case BlowDirection.Front:
                projectionAnimation = animation == DamageAnimation.Flinch
                    ? HumanAnimationConstants.FrontFlinchAnimations[random.Next(0, HumanAnimationConstants.FrontFlinchAnimations.Count - 1)]
                    : HumanAnimationConstants.FrontFallAnimations[random.Next(0, HumanAnimationConstants.FrontFallAnimations.Count - 1)];
                break;
            case BlowDirection.Right:
                projectionAnimation = animation == DamageAnimation.Flinch
                    ? HumanAnimationConstants.RightFlinchAnimations[random.Next(0, HumanAnimationConstants.RightFlinchAnimations.Count - 1)]
                    : HumanAnimationConstants.RightFallAnimations[random.Next(0, HumanAnimationConstants.RightFallAnimations.Count - 1)];
                break;
            case BlowDirection.Left:
            default:
                projectionAnimation = animation == DamageAnimation.Flinch
                    ? HumanAnimationConstants.LeftFlinchAnimations[random.Next(0, HumanAnimationConstants.LeftFlinchAnimations.Count - 1)]
                    : HumanAnimationConstants.LeftFallAnimations[random.Next(0, HumanAnimationConstants.LeftFallAnimations.Count - 1)];
                break;
        }
        var action = ActionIndexCache.Create(projectionAnimation);
        _agent.SetActionChannel(0, action, true, 0UL, 0f, 1, -0.2f, 0.4f, 0f, false, -0.2f, 0, true);
    }

    public bool IsAttackLikelyToHit(IAgentAdapter attacker, float coneAngle, float attackDistance)
    {
        if (attacker == null) return false;

        var attackerAgent = (attacker as AgentAdapter)?.GetUnderlyingAgent();
        if (attackerAgent == null) return false;

        var distanceToTarget = (_agent.Position - attackerAgent.Position).Length;
        var distanceForAttack = attackDistance + Math.Max(attackerAgent.MovementVelocity.Y, 0);
        if (distanceToTarget > distanceForAttack) return false;

        var halfConeAngleRadians = coneAngle * 0.5f * (float)(Math.PI / 180);
        var attackerLookDirection = attackerAgent.Frame.rotation.f.NormalizedCopy();
        var attackerToVictim = (_agent.Position - attackerAgent.Position).NormalizedCopy();
        var dotProduct = Vec3.DotProduct(attackerLookDirection, attackerToVictim);
        var angleBetween = (float)Math.Acos(dotProduct);

        return angleBetween <= halfConeAngleRadians;
    }

    public void CustomAttack(
        ActionIndexCache action,
        List<sbyte> bonesIdsForCollision,
        float actionProgressMin,
        float actionProgressMax,
        float targetDetectionRange,
        float boneCollisionRadius,
        bool stopOnFirstHit,
        Action<IAgentAdapter, IAgentAdapter, sbyte> onHitCallback,
        Action onExpirationCallback = null)
    {
        if (_agent == null || !_agent.IsActive() || _agent.IsFadingOut())
        {
            _logger.LogWarning("AgentAdapter:CustomAttack: attempt to use on a null or dead agent.");
            return;
        }

        _agent.SetActionChannel(0, action, true);

        if (SpatialGrid.Instance == null)
        {
            _logger.LogWarning("AgentAdapter:CustomAttack: SpatialGrid not initialized.");
            return;
        }

        // Filter rationale (2026-05-24 fix per #219 log evidence):
        //   agt != _agent            — exclude the warg itself
        //   agt != _agent.RiderAgent — exclude the warg's own rider. The original
        //       check `agt.RiderAgent != _agent` was a no-op for humans because
        //       Agent.RiderAgent is only populated on mounts (returns the rider).
        //       On a human rider it returns null, so the filter NEVER excluded
        //       the rider — the warg's bone collision was detecting its own
        //       rider as a target ~50% of the time, consuming the attack
        //       opportunity via stopOnFirstHit before reaching an enemy.
        //   agt.IsActive()           — alive check
        var targets = SpatialGrid.Instance.GetNearAliveAgentsInRange(targetDetectionRange, _agent)
            .FindAll(agt => agt != _agent && agt != _agent.RiderAgent && agt.IsActive())
            .Select(x => _factory.GetAgentAdapter(x))
            .ToList();

        if (targets.Count == 0) return;

        var boneCollisionService = _boneCollisionServiceFactory();
        boneCollisionService.AddBoneCheckComponent(new BoneCheckDuringAnimation(
            action,
            this,
            targets,
            bonesIdsForCollision,
            actionProgressMin,
            actionProgressMax,
            boneCollisionRadius,
            stopOnFirstHit,
            onHitCallback,
            onExpirationCallback
        ));
    }
}

using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using TaleWorlds.Library;
using TaleWorlds.MountAndBlade;

namespace TAOM.Features.AdvancedCombat;

public class SpatialGrid
{
    public static SpatialGrid Instance { get; internal set; }

    private readonly Dictionary<(int, int, int), List<Agent>> Grid = new();
    public float CellSize = 20f;

    public void UpdateGrid(List<Agent> agents)
    {
        Grid.Clear();
        foreach (Agent agent in agents)
        {
            if (!agent.IsActive())
                continue;
            var cell = GetCell(agent.Position);
            if (!Grid.TryGetValue(cell, out List<Agent> list))
            {
                list = new List<Agent>();
                Grid[cell] = list;
            }
            list.Add(agent);
        }
    }

    private (int, int, int) GetCell(Vec3 pos)
    {
        return (
            (int)Math.Floor(pos.x / CellSize),
            (int)Math.Floor(pos.y / CellSize),
            (int)Math.Floor(pos.z / CellSize)
        );
    }

    public List<Agent> GetAgentsInRadius(Vec3 center, float radius)
    {
        List<Agent> agents = new();
        float radiusSquared = radius * radius;
        int minX = (int)Math.Floor((center.x - radius) / CellSize);
        int maxX = (int)Math.Floor((center.x + radius) / CellSize);
        int minY = (int)Math.Floor((center.y - radius) / CellSize);
        int maxY = (int)Math.Floor((center.y + radius) / CellSize);
        int minZ = (int)Math.Floor((center.z - radius) / CellSize);
        int maxZ = (int)Math.Floor((center.z + radius) / CellSize);

        foreach (var kvp in Grid)
        {
            var key = kvp.Key;
            if (key.Item1 >= minX && key.Item1 <= maxX &&
                key.Item2 >= minY && key.Item2 <= maxY &&
                key.Item3 >= minZ && key.Item3 <= maxZ)
            {
                foreach (Agent agent in kvp.Value)
                {
                    float dx = agent.Position.x - center.x;
                    float dy = agent.Position.y - center.y;
                    float dz = agent.Position.z - center.z;
                    if (dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz <= radiusSquared)
                    {
                        agents.Add(agent);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        return agents;
    }

    public List<Agent> GetNearAliveAgentsInRange(float range, Agent target)
    {
        return GetAgentsInRadius(target.Position, range);
    }

    public List<Agent> GetNearAliveAgentsInRange(float range, Vec3 targetPos)
    {
        return GetAgentsInRadius(targetPos, range);
    }
}

using System.Collections.Generic;

namespace TAOM.Features.Spider;

public static class SpiderConfig
{
    // Object IDs — the recruitable troop anchor (humanoid race dg_uruk, so recruitment + roster
    // UI resolve) and the spider Monster it is swapped onto at spawn time by
    // Patch45_SpiderTroopSpawn (see SpiderTroopSpawnService).
    public const string SpiderMonsterId = "spider";
    public const string SpiderCharacterId = "taom_spider_creature";

    // Combat behavior
    internal static float TargetDetectionRange = 4f;
    internal static int SleepAfterAttack = 2;

    // Damage formula (mirrors WargConfig shape)
    public const float SpeedForMaxDamage = 15f;
    public const int MaxSpeedDamage = 15;
    public const int MaxBaseDamage = 35;
    public const int DamageToFlinch = 8;
    public const int DamageToFall = 30;

    // Bone indices for fang/bite collision points.
    // PLACEHOLDER values copied from warg pattern (chest 23, jaw 37, fangs 43).
    // Codex review #spider-2026-04-23 confirmed these are FUNCTIONAL placeholders
    // (not cosmetic) — bites only land when the indexed spider bones are within
    // 0.3-0.4f of target bones. With wrong indices, mouth-over-target contact may
    // miss while leg/body contact may erroneously hit. Refine after a runtime
    // bone-index dump that resolves joint5_l, joint5_r, joint12_m on as_spider.
    public const sbyte FangBoneIndexPrimary = 23;
    public const sbyte FangBoneIndexSecondaryLeft = 37;
    public const sbyte FangBoneIndexSecondaryRight = 43;

    // Pre-allocated bone-index lists for SpiderAttackService.SpiderAttack —
    // avoids per-attack list allocation on the BT tick path.
    // Note: List<sbyte> rather than IReadOnlyList<sbyte> because IAgentAdapter.CustomAttack
    // requires a concrete List<sbyte>. Treat as immutable; never call .Add/.Remove.
    public static readonly List<sbyte> ChargeAttackBones = new List<sbyte> { FangBoneIndexPrimary };
    public static readonly List<sbyte> StandAttackBones = new List<sbyte>
    {
        FangBoneIndexPrimary, FangBoneIndexSecondaryLeft, FangBoneIndexSecondaryRight,
    };
}

# Spider

> **Status (2026-06-04): ENABLED — recruitable troop.** The giant spider is a recruitable Dol Guldur troop that spawns + fights as the spider Monster in every battle via a `Mission.SpawnAgent` monster-swap. This supersedes the earlier rideable-mount + Custom-Battle-scatter design (both removed — see "History" below).
>
> For the skeleton / mesh / animation authoring pipeline (the in-Blender + Modding-Kit side), the current source of truth is [`docs/features/spider-skeleton-animation-pipeline.md`](spider-skeleton-animation-pipeline.md). This doc covers the **gameplay** side (how the spider gets into battle as a troop).

## Overview

Giant spiders are a recruitable troop of Dol Guldur. Bannerlord cannot host a non-humanoid creature as an ordinary `NPCCharacter` (the `race=` field resolves against a humanoid-only `skins.xml`), so the troop uses a **humanoid anchor** (`taom_spider_creature`, `race="dg_uruk"`) for everything the troop system needs — recruitment, party roster, UI — and a thin Harmony prefix swaps the agent's body to the spider **Monster** at spawn time. The recruit shows a humanoid silhouette in the party roster but spawns and fights as a giant spider in battle.

## Why This Exists

LOTR combat needs Mirkwood / Dol-Guldur giant spiders, but the engine offers no direct way to make a non-humanoid creature a recruitable troop. Two earlier approaches were tried and abandoned:

- **Rideable mount** (spider as a `HorseItem` ridden by an uruk) — abandoned because (1) a mounted creature gets a campaign-map party icon, and building that icon calls `Skeleton.ForceUpdateBoneFrames()` which threw an `AccessViolationException` (a hard, game-breaking crash on entering the open world), and (2) a single skinned mesh has a native per-draw-call bone limit (~40–58) that the spider's 8-leg mesh exceeds, so only 4 legs rendered.
- **C# scatter spawn** (rider-less spiders auto-spawned 1s into a Custom Battle) — only a smoke test; never a real gameplay path.

The recruitable-troop approach sidesteps the mount crash entirely (a troop never becomes a mount, so it never gets a map icon → never hits `ForceUpdateBoneFrames`) and puts the spider on the normal live-agent spawn path.

## Architecture

### Design challenge

`Mission.SpawnAgent(AgentBuildData)` needs a `BasicCharacterObject` anchor, and the troop XML pipeline rejects `race="spider"` at load. The fix: a humanoid anchor character (`taom_spider_creature`, `race="dg_uruk"`) carries the troop through recruitment/roster/UI, then a Harmony prefix on the universal spawn chokepoint rewrites the agent body to the spider Monster.

### Solution

```
Dol Guldur notable volunteers (VolunteerRecruitmentService, weight 1)
                    │ player/AI recruits "Giant Spider"
                    ▼
        party roster holds taom_spider_creature (humanoid anchor)
                    │ battle starts → Mission.SpawnAgent(agentBuildData) per troop
                    ▼
   Patch45_SpiderTroopSpawn (Prefix on Mission.SpawnAgent, always returns true)
                    │ delegates to
        ISpiderTroopSpawnService.TryApplySpiderMonsterSwap
                    │  if AgentCharacter.StringId == "taom_spider_creature":
                    │     agentBuildData.Monster(spider).NoHorses(true).NoWeapons(true)
                    ▼
        vanilla SpawnAgent runs with the spider Monster (skeleton + as_spider animations)
                    │ OnAgentBuild fires
                    ▼
   SpiderMissionBehavior attaches SpiderTree BT to every IsSpider() agent
        (vanilla formation AI moves it; the BT drives its bite — a monster body has no vanilla melee)
                    ▼
        SpiderAttackService (CustomAttack via fang bones; bone-collision through the
        shared IBoneCollisionService singleton that AdvancedCombatBehavior ticks)
```

- **Patch45 is thin + fail-safe:** it never skips vanilla (always returns `true`), null-guards the service, and only mutates `agentBuildData` for the one spider troop. It co-exists with `Patch23_BannerColorPersistence` on `Mission.SpawnAgent` (both return `true`).
- **The service is unit-testable:** the sealed `AgentBuildData`/`Monster` stay at the patch boundary; the is-spider check, the Monster lookup, and the mutation are injected delegates so the decision logic is fully mockable. Missing Monster ⇒ fail-open (log + spawn the humanoid anchor, no crash).

## Recruitment

`taom_spider_creature` is added at **weight 1** to the four Dol Guldur settlement pools (`town_DG1`, `castle_DG1`–`castle_DG3`) and the `dolguldur` culture fallback in `VolunteerRecruitmentService`. It is deliberately **absent from the clan-path pool**. Because settlement pools feed both player and AI recruitment, AI Dol Guldur lords may occasionally field a spider too (thematic, rare). `level="21"` maps to Tier 4, which is ≤ `MaxVolunteerTier` (6), so the spider is genuinely offerable as a volunteer.

## Configuration

| File / Class | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `Main/Features/Spider/SpiderConfig.cs` | Object-ID constants (`SpiderMonsterId="spider"`, `SpiderCharacterId="taom_spider_creature"`), combat tuning (`TargetDetectionRange`, damage formula), and the fang bone indices (placeholders: 23/37/43) + pre-allocated bone-list arrays |
| `Main/_Module/ModuleData/characters/spider_creature.xml` | The recruitable anchor `<NPCCharacter id="taom_spider_creature">` — `race="dg_uruk"`, `level="21"`, Athletics/OneHanded/Polearm skills, `occupation="Wanderer"` (keeps it out of the Custom-Battle picker), `is_basic_troop="false"`, `hidden_in_encyclopedia="true"`, empty equipment |
| `Main/Features/TroopProgression/VolunteerRecruitmentService.cs` | Dol Guldur settlement + culture pools include the spider (weight 1) |
| `LOTRLOME_Armory/ModuleData/Monsters/LOTR/lotr_monster_spider.xml` | `<Monster id="spider" action_set="as_spider" monster_usage="spider">` (62 bones) |
| `LOTRLOME_Armory/ModuleData/Animations/action_sets_spider.xml` + `action_types_spider.xml` + `MonsterUsage/LOTR/lotr_monster_usage_spider.xml` | The `as_spider` action set, `act_spider_*` types, and AI movement/strike template — see [spider-skeleton-animation-pipeline.md](spider-skeleton-animation-pipeline.md) |

## Key Files

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `Main/Features/Spider/ISpiderTroopSpawnService.cs` / `SpiderTroopSpawnService.cs` | Decision + monster-swap; sealed types isolated behind injected delegates |
| `Main/Features/Spider/Hooks/Mission_SpawnAgent_SpiderSwap_Patch.cs` | `Patch45_SpiderTroopSpawn` — thin prefix, delegates to the service |
| `Main/Features/Spider/SpiderMissionBehavior.cs` | `MissionLogic` — attaches `SpiderTree` BT to `IsSpider()` agents; owns `SpatialGrid`/bone-collision only when no other combat behavior (AdvancedCombat, Warg) already does |
| `Main/Features/Spider/SpiderBehaviorTree.cs` + `BehaviorTreeElements/*` | BT: no-enemy-near → sleep, else → `SpiderAttackTask` |
| `Main/Features/Spider/ISpiderAttackService.cs` / `SpiderAttackService.cs` | Bite damage calc + `CustomAttack` (takes `IAgentAdapter`) |
| `Main/Features/Spider/SpiderConfig.cs` / `SpiderIoC.cs` | Static config / DryIoc registration |
| `Main/Adapters/AgentAdapter.cs` | `IsSpider()` (`Monster.StringId == "spider"`) + combat helpers |
| `Main/IoC.cs` / `Main/SubModule.cs` | Feature registration + Patch45 `Initialize` + `PatchCategory` + `AddMissionBehavior` |

## Dependencies

- **`LOTRLOME_Armory`** — provides the spider Monster, `as_spider` action set, skeleton, mesh, animations. The Monster is resolved by a **runtime** lookup at spawn (all modules are loaded by battle time), and the service fail-opens if it is missing, so load order is not load-bearing for the spider specifically. (TAOM as a whole relies on LOTRLOME_Armory being installed + enabled for its item set; it is not currently declared in `SubModule.xml` `DependedModules` — a pre-existing whole-mod matter.)
- **`Main/Features/AdvancedCombat`** — `IBoneCollisionService` (singleton, ticked by `AdvancedCombatBehavior`), `SpatialGrid`, `CustomAttack`.
- **`BehaviorTrees` + `BehaviorTreeWrapper`** — BT framework (inlined into `TAOM.dll`).

## Tests

- `TAOM.Tests/Features/Spider/SpiderTroopSpawnServiceTests.cs` — 5 tests: non-spider → no swap, null id, spider + missing Monster → fail-open + log, spider + Monster present → swap applied, ctor smoke.
- `TAOM.Tests/Features/Spider/SpiderAttackServiceTests.cs` — 14 tests (damage formula + skip-guard exhaustion).
- `TAOM.Tests/Features/TroopProgression/VolunteerRecruitmentServiceTests.cs` — spider pool coverage (4 settlements + culture return the spider on max roll; clan-path pool excludes it).
- BT nodes + `SpiderMissionBehavior` + the actual `Monster()` swap are engine-coupled (in-game smoke test).

## Asset Pipeline (Maya → Bannerlord)

> The skeleton/clip work is now documented in [spider-skeleton-animation-pipeline.md](spider-skeleton-animation-pipeline.md) (the proven `spider_skeleton` 62-bone recipe). The legacy Maya→Blender workflow below remains valid background for any future non-humanoid creature.

The canonical authoring path for a creature's mesh + skeleton + animations:

1. **Export mesh + skeleton from Maya, import into Blender** (Maya = rigging source, Blender = cleanup + export).
2. **Clean transforms, remove unused bones, fix armature name** — eliminates rest-pose drift; strips un-keyframed tip/claw bones; applies the `_notused` convention to the animation skeleton (e.g. `spider_skeleton_notused`) so the Modding Kit auto-creates Animation Clip wrappers.
3. **Import animations from Maya as a separate source armature** (don't overwrite the cleaned target).
4. **Bake animations source→target** via `tools/blender_bone_retargeter.py` (Scan Target Bones → Apply Loc/Rot Constraints → Bake Animation).
5. **Export to Bannerlord** as FBX, one animation per FBX with mesh/skin disabled.

`SkeletonUserData` (ragdoll) and `Usage='horse'` are authored post-import (Skeleton Editor or `tools/tpac_skeleton_transplant.py`).

## How-To

### Recruit + test a spider in-game

1. `./build.ps1 -RunTests` — confirm green.
2. Launch Bannerlord with TAOM + LOTRLOME_Armory enabled (LOTRLOME_Armory loaded before TAOM).
3. Visit a Dol Guldur town/castle (`town_DG1`, `castle_DG1`–`3`) and recruit from a notable — "Giant Spider" appears in the volunteer list at low frequency.
4. Take the spider to any battle. Watch `rgl_log.txt` for `[Spider] Initialized` + `[Spider] Attached behavior trees to N spiders`.
5. Visual checks: the agent spawns as a spider (not a humanoid uruk), all 8 legs render, it walks toward enemies, bites, and dies without crashing.

### Tune combat / recruitment

- Bite damage / detection: `Main/Features/Spider/SpiderConfig.cs` (`MaxBaseDamage`, `SpeedForMaxDamage`, `TargetDetectionRange`). Rebuild to apply.
- Recruitment frequency: the `("taom_spider_creature", N)` weights in `VolunteerRecruitmentService.InitializeDolGuldurSettlements` / `InitializeDolGuldurCulture`.

### Refine fang bone indices

`SpiderConfig.FangBoneIndex*` are placeholders (23/37/43) copied from the warg. To get the real indices: spawn one spider, add a temporary log in `SpiderMissionBehavior.OnAgentBuild` iterating the agent's skeleton bones (`index → name`), find `joint5_l`, `joint5_r`, `joint12_m`, update `SpiderConfig`, remove the log.

## Known Issues / Open Items

- **Live-agent render unproven** — the 4-legs-vs-8 per-mesh bone limit was the mount-path symptom; whether the live-agent spawn path renders all 8 legs needs an in-game test. If it still clips, the fix is a multi-mesh split (the warg's `<AdditionalMeshes>` pattern), since the limit is per-mesh not per-skeleton.
- **Fang bone indices are placeholders** — bites may land off-target until a runtime bone dump.
- **Humanoid roster silhouette** — the recruit shows the `dg_uruk` anchor in the party roster (the visual is only swapped at battle spawn). Accepted tradeoff of the anchor approach.
- **AI lords field spiders** — settlement pools feed AI recruitment too, so Dol Guldur lords may bring the occasional spider. Intended (thematic, rare at weight 1); tune the weight or move to a player-only mechanism if undesired.

## History

- **2026-06-04** — re-enabled as a recruitable troop (this doc). Removed the rideable mount (`dg_giant_spider_rider`, spider mount items) + the C# scatter-spawn smoke test (`SpiderSpawnerService`).
- **2026-05-14** — feature disabled in-place (mount + scatter design).
- **2026-04-23** — original spider Monster + skeleton + animations from `LOTRLOME_Armory`.

# RCA — Recruitable Giant Spider Troop (2026-06-04)

## Summary

Deep-review (5 agents) of the recruitable-spider-troop feature found **no correctness bugs** and **one minor style finding** (an ADR-002 entry-point line-count overage), fixed in-session. The high-blast-radius risks were all verified clean: the `Mission.SpawnAgent` chokepoint prefix is fail-safe (always returns `true`, null-guarded), it coexists with Patch23_BannerColorPersistence (both return `true`), bites work in real campaign battles via the shared `IBoneCollisionService` singleton that `AdvancedCombatBehavior` ticks, and the level-21 spider (Tier 4) is below MaxVolunteerTier 6 so it is genuinely offerable as a volunteer. Build + 3030/3032 tests green.

## Findings

| # | Sev | Finding | Category | Why missed | Preventive action |
|---|-----|---------|----------|------------|-------------------|
| 1 | LOW | `SpiderMissionBehavior.cs` 153 lines > ADR-002 "<150" ceiling | Style / Critical-Rule ceiling | Gutting the scatter-spawn path took the file 201→153; I verified behavior + delegation, not `wc -l` against the 150 ceiling | After editing an entry-point class (MissionBehavior / Patch / GameModel / CampaignBehavior), `wc -l` it against 150. One-off; no new rule needed. |
| 2 | (overstated) | Agent 4 rated "LOTRLOME_Armory absent from `SubModule.xml` DependedModules" as CRITICAL ("Monster load fails at runtime") | Review-process / false-severity | Agent 4 assumed declared load-order affects a runtime lookup | Resolved by evidence-over-claims — see Notes. Not a spider bug; pre-existing whole-mod matter, not bundled into this feature. |

## Notes

- **Finding 2 is the valuable process datapoint.** The deep-review's own "when two agents disagree, that's signal" rule fired: Agent 4 (Completeness) called the missing LOTRLOME dependency CRITICAL, while Agent 5 (Data Flow) traced the Monster null-path as a graceful fail-open. The disagreement forced a mechanism check — the spider Monster is resolved by a **runtime** `MBObjectManager.GetObject<Monster>("spider")` at agent-spawn time, by which point every enabled module is loaded regardless of declared order; and the service already fail-opens (logs + spawns the humanoid anchor) if it is absent. So the declared dependency is load-order-irrelevant for the spider. The general lesson: "module X owns entity Y" does **not** imply a load-time cross-module dependency when the consumer is a runtime lookup. TAOM has never declared LOTRLOME_Armory despite using its items everywhere, and ships fine — a pre-existing whole-mod observation, surfaced for the user, deliberately not fixed inside this surgical feature.
- **No systemic / repeat-offender pattern.** Finding 1 is a one-off ceiling miss, not a recurring class (unlike the NaN-gate trio). No new feedback memory warranted.

## Prior design dead-end — the rideable-mount crash (the real "never again" lesson)

Before the troop approach, the spider was built as a **rideable mount** (creature-as-HorseItem, `dg_giant_spider_rider`). It was fully reversed because it failed two ways:

1. **Campaign-map crash (game-breaking):** a mounted creature gets a map party icon; building it calls `Skeleton.ForceUpdateBoneFrames()` (via `MobilePartyVisual.AddMobileIconComponents` → `RefreshPartyIcon`), which threw `AccessViolationException` on entering the open world. This path exists ONLY for mounts.
2. **Per-mesh bone-render limit:** a single skinned Mesh has a native ~40–58 per-draw-call bone cap; the 8-leg spider mesh exceeded it (only 4 legs rendered). `Skeleton.MaxBoneCount=64` is a separate (skeleton) cap; the fix would be a multi-mesh split (warg `<AdditionalMeshes>`).

**Preventive (cross-session):** memory `feedback_nonhumanoid_creature_troop_not_mount` — any future non-humanoid creature is a recruitable troop via the `Mission.SpawnAgent` monster-swap, never a mount. The troop path never gets a map icon (no `ForceUpdateBoneFrames`) and spawns on the live-agent path. Also captured in `docs/features/spider.md` "Why This Exists". This is the systemic lesson; the troop feature's own deep-review (above) was clean.

## Human-seam items (not review findings — require in-game verification)

- **Live-agent render:** whether the spider shows all 8 legs. The per-mesh bone-render limit was the *mount-path* symptom (4 of 8 legs); it is unproven on the *live-agent* spawn path and can only be confirmed by recruiting a spider and taking it to battle.
- **Fang bone indices (23/37/43)** are documented placeholders copied from the warg — bites may land on the wrong contact points until a runtime bone dump resolves the real `joint5_l/r` / `joint12_m` indices on `as_spider`.

C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\TAOM_bodyproperties.xml:82: id="fighter_dolguldur">
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:201: <string id="taom_cc_taom_parent_dolguldur_1_text" text="{=taom_cc_taom_parent_dolguldur_1_text}Servants of the Necromancer" />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:203: <string id="taom_cc_taom_parent_dolguldur_1_desc" text="{=taom_cc_taom_parent_dolguldur_1_desc}Your family served directly under the Necromancer, performing his dark bidding and enforcing his will across the region." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:205: <string id="taom_cc_taom_parent_dolguldur_2_text" text="{=taom_cc_taom_parent_dolguldur_2_text}Crafters of Shadowed Steel" />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:207: <string id="taom_cc_taom_parent_dolguldur_2_desc" text="{=taom_cc_taom_parent_dolguldur_2_desc}Your family forged weapons and armor imbued with the dark magic of Dol Guldur, equipping its armies for conquest." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:209: <string id="taom_cc_taom_parent_dolguldur_3_text" text="{=taom_cc_taom_parent_dolguldur_3_text}Miners of the Shadowed Halls" />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:211: <string id="taom_cc_taom_parent_dolguldur_3_desc" text="{=taom_cc_taom_parent_dolguldur_3_desc}Your family labored deep within the caverns of Dol Guldur, extracting resources to feed its war machine." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:213: <string id="taom_cc_taom_parent_dolguldur_4_text" text="{=taom_cc_taom_parent_dolguldur_4_text}Warriors of the Enchanted Wood" />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:215: <string id="taom_cc_taom_parent_dolguldur_4_desc" text="{=taom_cc_taom_parent_dolguldur_4_desc}Your family were fierce warriors who fought to extend the shadow of Dol Guldur over the surrounding lands." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:217: <string id="taom_cc_taom_parent_dolguldur_5_text" text="{=taom_cc_taom_parent_dolguldur_5_text}Hunters of the Dark Forest" />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:219: <string id="taom_cc_taom_parent_dolguldur_5_desc" text="{=taom_cc_taom_parent_dolguldur_5_desc}Your family hunted the twisted creatures of the forest and tracked those who dared trespass into the Necromancer's domain." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:221: <string id="taom_cc_taom_parent_dolguldur_6_text" text="{=taom_cc_taom_parent_dolguldur_6_text}Rogues of Dol Guldur" />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:223: <string id="taom_cc_taom_parent_dolguldur_6_desc" text="{=taom_cc_taom_parent_dolguldur_6_desc}Your family were spies and saboteurs, spreading the influence of Dol Guldur through deception and fear." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:601: <string id="taom_cc_taom_youth_dolguldur_1_text" text="{=taom_cc_taom_youth_dolguldur_1_text}Served the Necromancer's riders." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:603: <string id="taom_cc_taom_youth_dolguldur_1_desc" text="{=taom_cc_taom_youth_dolguldur_1_desc}You rode in the service of Dol Guldur, commanding dark steeds and spreading terror across the southern reaches of Mirkwood." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:605: <string id="taom_cc_taom_youth_dolguldur_2_text" text="{=taom_cc_taom_youth_dolguldur_2_text}Guarded the halls of shadow." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:607: <string id="taom_cc_taom_youth_dolguldur_2_desc" text="{=taom_cc_taom_youth_dolguldur_2_desc}You defended the dark halls of Dol Guldur, standing watch over the Necromancer's domain with bow and blade." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:609: <string id="taom_cc_taom_youth_dolguldur_3_text" text="{=taom_cc_taom_youth_dolguldur_3_text}Trained in the dark arts of war." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:611: <string id="taom_cc_taom_youth_dolguldur_3_desc" text="{=taom_cc_taom_youth_dolguldur_3_desc}You honed your skills in the dark arts of warfare, learning to fight with cunning and deception in the shadowed corridors of Dol Guldur." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:613: <string id="taom_cc_taom_youth_dolguldur_4_text" text="{=taom_cc_taom_youth_dolguldur_4_text}Hunted trespassers in the corrupted Greenwood." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:615: <string id="taom_cc_taom_youth_dolguldur_4_desc" text="{=taom_cc_taom_youth_dolguldur_4_desc}You were sent into the twisted undergrowth of southern Mirkwood to track and eliminate those who strayed near the Necromancer's domain, learning to stalk quarry through corrupted forest without making a sound or leaving a print." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:617: <string id="taom_cc_taom_youth_dolguldur_5_text" text="{=taom_cc_taom_youth_dolguldur_5_text}Marched in the shadow legions of Dol Guldur." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:619: <string id="taom_cc_taom_youth_dolguldur_5_desc" text="{=taom_cc_taom_youth_dolguldur_5_desc}You drilled in the iron-disciplined ranks of Dol Guldur's dark legions, learning to wield heavy weapons in formation as the corruption of the Necromancer's fortress settled into your stride and your silence." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:621: <string id="taom_cc_taom_youth_dolguldur_6_text" text="{=taom_cc_taom_youth_dolguldur_6_text}Moved through darkness as a courier of the Necromancer." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:623: <string id="taom_cc_taom_youth_dolguldur_6_desc" text="{=taom_cc_taom_youth_dolguldur_6_desc}You carried messages through the corrupted wood that no one would write down, delivering them by hand to agents who never showed their faces. The work demanded silence, patience, and the ability to strike without warning when the shadow required it." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:915: <string id="taom_cc_taom_education_mirkwood_6_desc" text="{=taom_cc_taom_education_mirkwood_6_desc}You kept irregular company with the patrols that roamed outside Thranduil's formal borders, learning to set traps and ambushes for the spider-kin and Orc scouts that tested the Woodland Realm's edges. Cunning kept you alive where courage alone would not." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:989: <string id="taom_cc_taom_education_dolguldur_1_text" text="{=taom_cc_taom_education_dolguldur_1_text}Drilled in the shadow-yards of Dol Guldur." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:991: <string id="taom_cc_taom_education_dolguldur_1_desc" text="{=taom_cc_taom_education_dolguldur_1_desc}You trained in the lightless courtyards of the Necromancer's fortress, learning to fight with halberd and great blade under the eye of hooded overseers. The shadow that lay across the place seeped into your bones and sharpened your instincts for violence." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:993: <string id="taom_cc_taom_education_dolguldur_2_text" text="{=taom_cc_taom_education_dolguldur_2_text}Forged shadow-steel in the dark workshops." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:995: <string id="taom_cc_taom_education_dolguldur_2_desc" text="{=taom_cc_taom_education_dolguldur_2_desc}You worked the black-iron forges of Dol Guldur, learning to shape weapons under conditions that would break a lesser youth. The materials were dark and the methods darker, and you left with knowledge that few would admit to having." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:997: <string id="taom_cc_taom_education_dolguldur_3_text" text="{=taom_cc_taom_education_dolguldur_3_text}Hauled stone in the caverns of the fortress." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:999: <string id="taom_cc_taom_education_dolguldur_3_desc" text="{=taom_cc_taom_education_dolguldur_3_desc}You labored in the underground excavations of Dol Guldur, dragging blocks and shoring tunnels in the permanent darkness beneath the corrupted hill. The work was relentless, and endurance was the only currency that bought any relief." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:1001: <string id="taom_cc_taom_education_dolguldur_4_text" text="{=taom_cc_taom_education_dolguldur_4_text}Fought in the shadow-patrols of the Enchanted Wood." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:1003: <string id="taom_cc_taom_education_dolguldur_4_desc" text="{=taom_cc_taom_education_dolguldur_4_desc}You ran with the dark patrols that pushed the corruption of Dol Guldur further into southern Mirkwood, cutting down resistance with axe and spear. Each foray took you deeper into the twisted forest and left less of your former self behind." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:1005: <string id="taom_cc_taom_education_dolguldur_5_text" text="{=taom_cc_taom_education_dolguldur_5_text}Hunted the dark forest's edges." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:1007: <string id="taom_cc_taom_education_dolguldur_5_desc" text="{=taom_cc_taom_education_dolguldur_5_desc}You tracked through the corrupted undergrowth of southern Mirkwood, killing any creature that came too close to the fortress and learning to move without making a sound in a forest that twisted every trail. Your eyes adjusted to a world without sunlight." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:1009: <string id="taom_cc_taom_education_dolguldur_6_text" text="{=taom_cc_taom_education_dolguldur_6_text}Moved through shadows as a spy of the Necromancer." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:1011: <string id="taom_cc_taom_education_dolguldur_6_desc" text="{=taom_cc_taom_education_dolguldur_6_desc}You were used as a courier and agent in the Necromancer's network, carrying messages through the dark wood and delivering them to contacts who never showed their faces. You learned that shadows were your armor and silence your best weapon." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:1281: <string id="taom_cc_taom_adulthood_mirkwood_1_text" text="{=taom_cc_taom_adulthood_mirkwood_1_text}You captured a spider-queen that had been terrorising the southern paths." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:1287: <string id="taom_cc_taom_adulthood_mirkwood_2_desc" text="{=taom_cc_taom_adulthood_mirkwood_2_desc}The road had been effectively closed for two seasons by spider and Orc harassment. You mapped the safest remaining corridors, negotiated guard arrangements with Thranduil's captain, and led the first merchant convoy through to success. Trade resumed within the month." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:1301: <string id="taom_cc_taom_adulthood_mirkwood_6_text" text="{=taom_cc_taom_adulthood_mirkwood_6_text}You freed three Elven captives from a spider web-hold by yourself." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:1303: <string id="taom_cc_taom_adulthood_mirkwood_6_desc" text="{=taom_cc_taom_adulthood_mirkwood_6_desc}The scouts had been taken deep in the corrupted southern wood where the patrols would not go. You went alone at night, cut them free, and led them out through three spider-guarded paths. Two of them asked how you knew the way. You told them it was instinct." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:1377: <string id="taom_cc_taom_adulthood_dolguldur_1_text" text="{=taom_cc_taom_adulthood_dolguldur_1_text}You commanded the patrol that first broke through Mirkwood's northern defences." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:1379: <string id="taom_cc_taom_adulthood_dolguldur_1_desc" text="{=taom_cc_taom_adulthood_dolguldur_1_desc}The Elven border wardens had held the approach for two seasons. You identified the gap in their rotation, timed your crossing to the minute, and brought your patrol through and back without a casualty. The shadow-masters noted your report and gave you a permanent command." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:1381: <string id="taom_cc_taom_adulthood_dolguldur_2_text" text="{=taom_cc_taom_adulthood_dolguldur_2_text}You forged shadow-steel weapons that passed Sauron's quality inspection." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:1383: <string id="taom_cc_taom_adulthood_dolguldur_2_desc" text="{=taom_cc_taom_adulthood_dolguldur_2_desc}The Necromancer's inspectors had rejected two previous batches from the fortress's smiths. You reworked the smelting process, accepted no compromise on the quench, and delivered a batch that the inspector examined in silence before marking as approved. It was the first such approval in three years." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:1385: <string id="taom_cc_taom_adulthood_dolguldur_3_text" text="{=taom_cc_taom_adulthood_dolguldur_3_text}You completed the expansion of the fortress's lowest dungeon level." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:1387: <string id="taom_cc_taom_adulthood_dolguldur_3_desc" text="{=taom_cc_taom_adulthood_dolguldur_3_desc}The work had stalled for a season due to seeping groundwater and failing supports. You redesigned the drainage, replaced the compromised timbers, and completed the level on the revised schedule. The Necromancer's overseers moved prisoners in the same week." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:1389: <string id="taom_cc_taom_adulthood_dolguldur_4_text" text="{=taom_cc_taom_adulthood_dolguldur_4_text}You broke through the Elven outer watch and took a prisoner for questioning." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:1391: <string id="taom_cc_taom_adulthood_dolguldur_4_desc" text="{=taom_cc_taom_adulthood_dolguldur_4_desc}The intelligence taken from the Elven warden described the full rotation of Thranduil's eastern border patrol. It was the most useful strategic information Dol Guldur had received in a year. No one asked how you got the prisoner out. You did not explain." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:1393: <string id="taom_cc_taom_adulthood_dolguldur_5_text" text="{=taom_cc_taom_adulthood_dolguldur_5_text}You mapped the Elven patrol routes in southern Mirkwood over six months." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:1395: <string id="taom_cc_taom_adulthood_dolguldur_5_desc" text="{=taom_cc_taom_adulthood_dolguldur_5_desc}Working alone and over multiple seasons, you built a complete picture of Thranduil's southern border dispositions. The map that resulted gave Dol Guldur's planners something they had never had before: certainty. The Necromancer's agents used it for two years." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:1397: <string id="taom_cc_taom_adulthood_dolguldur_6_text" text="{=taom_cc_taom_adulthood_dolguldur_6_text}You infiltrated the Elvenking's court as a trader and reported what you heard." />
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_cc_strings.xml:1399: <string id="taom_cc_taom_adulthood_dolguldur_6_desc" text="{=taom_cc_taom_adulthood_dolguldur_6_desc}Three months in Thranduil's halls under a false identity gave you access to conversations that no agent of Dol Guldur had ever overheard. You came back with names, plans, and relationships that the shadow-masters used to shape the next season's strategy. You found the experience unexpectedly informative about Elves." />

C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_module_strings.xml:242: <string id="str_culture_description.dolguldur" text="{=taom_str_culture_description.dolguldur}The minions of Dol Guldur, under the command of the Necromancer, are a dark and sinister force. Hidden within the corrupted forest of Mirkwood, they employ treachery and shadow to weaken their enemies. Orcs, wargs, and other foul creatures march forth to spread fear and decay across Middle-earth." />

C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_spcultures.xml:2587: text="{=aom_dolguldur_desc}Dol Guldur is a fortress of shadow and malice. Once a stronghold of Sauron in Mirkwood, it is now ruled by the Necromancer's dark lieutenants. The armies of Dol Guldur are a fearsome blend of orcs, wargs, and dark sorcery. C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_spkingdoms.xml:640: text="{=taom_dolguldur_desc}Dol Guldur, the fortress of shadow and despair, stands as a menacing beacon of the Necromancer's dark will. The Orcs and foul creatures that inhabit its depths strike fear into the hearts of all.">

C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_wanderer_skill_sets.xml:2065: <SkillSet id="spc_wanderer_dolguldur_2_skills">
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_wanderer_skill_sets.xml:2085: <SkillSet id="spc_wanderer_dolguldur_3_skills">
C:\Users\mikew\source\repos\TAOM\Main\_Module\ModuleData\taom_wanderer_skill_sets.xml:2105: <SkillSet id="spc_wanderer_dolguldur_4_skills">
